Memory/runtime risk: board memory and runtime artifacts are named, but address map, DDR image layout, runtime ABI, and transfer counts are not validated in visible evidence.
Board/deployment risk: target board profile and tool availability exist, but there is no real backend/app-shell target discovery or Vivado evidence; backend target names must not be guessed.
Tool-protocol risk: tool_protocols exists, but required checker execution and artifact trust boundaries are not yet materialized for this gate.
Human-boundary risk: human_agent_boundary has approval_required, auto_allowed, and forbidden sections, but detailed approval conditions are not visible; policy-changing repairs must be gated.
SACG-quality risk: extracting the graph before audit reports pass could encode unverified assumptions as constraints and contaminate downstream design stages.
split_reason: The input_preparation stage spans independent model/shape, numeric/template, board/runtime/tool, and human-boundary/evidence concerns before SACG extraction. These inputs can be audited in parallel by specialist chip-design roles, then gated by a cross-layer evidence auditor to prevent contaminated or incomplete inputs from entering SACG construction.
